## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

# Re-anchor a visible tooltip without re-arming the hover-intent dwell

**Headline:** The shared `TooltipManager` gains an additive re-anchor call so a host can
keep an **already visible** delayed tooltip under a moving pointer — without scheduling a
second dwell, without re-rendering its content and without a hide/re-show flicker. The
Rising needs it to satisfy `RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH` AC3 ("an already-shown tooltip keeps
following the pointer").

> **Provenance:** discovered while auditing the game-side opt-in
> `RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH` ("Delay tooltips by 1.5"). That audit returned
> `Ready to close: No`: the dwell/cancel rules are met, but once the delayed overlay is
> visible the host has no supported way to move it, so the tooltip freezes at the anchor
> captured when the dwell fired. This item is the engine half of the fix, following the
> producer decision recorded on the game item (Q1 = C: timing behaviour lives in the
> engine, the game only supplies configuration and routes input).

## Problem statement

`TooltipManager` (see `CG-0MWNGS2F90049LIG`, the hover-intent delay) has two anchor
states and no third:

- **pending** — `show()` schedules a `delayedCall`; a repeated `show()` while pending
  refreshes content and anchor without restarting the dwell, so the overlay appears at
  the live pointer.
- **rendered** — the overlay is up; a further `show()` schedules a **new** dwell (the
  overlay stays frozen at its old anchor until that dwell fires and re-renders it), and
  `hide()` tears it down.

So a host that wants a visible tooltip to keep following the pointer has no option that
behaves correctly: re-issuing `show()` leaves the overlay stale for a whole extra delay
and then re-renders it, while `hide()` + `show()` removes and re-creates the overlay
(a visible flicker) and also waits out a fresh dwell. The alternative — giving the
manager a 0 ms delay and re-implementing hover intent in the game — contradicts the
producer's decision that the timing rule lives in the engine.

## Users

- **Game developers (host scenes).** Need a supported, tested way to track a target with
  an already-visible delayed tooltip (drag-free pointer movement inside one target).
- **Players.** A tooltip that appears after a deliberate dwell should then stay with the
  pointer, not freeze in place while the pointer moves across the same card.
- **Maintainers.** One engine-owned re-anchor rule with tests, instead of each host
  inventing workarounds (double managers, hide/show flicker) that re-introduce the
  timing bugs the delay work removed.

## Desired behaviour

- A new public method on `TooltipManager` (name illustrative: `reanchor(x, y)`) moves the
  tooltip's anchor to `(x, y)`:
  - with a show **pending**, it refreshes the pending anchor exactly as a repeated
    `show()` does today — the dwell is **not** restarted;
  - with the overlay **visible**, it repositions the overlay immediately, re-using the
    same placement rules `show()` uses (DOM mode: canvas/camera mapping plus the existing
    viewport clamp/flip; Phaser mode: the container position), with **no** content
    re-render, **no** destroy/re-create and therefore **no** flicker;
  - with nothing pending and nothing visible, it is a **no-op** — it never renders a
    tooltip and never schedules a show.
- `SettingsPanel.showTooltips === false` keeps working unchanged: a re-anchor never makes
  a suppressed tooltip appear, and a visible overlay is still removed by the existing
  suppression path in `show()`/`hide()`.
- `delayMs`/`touchDelayMs` defaults (0 ms) and every existing behaviour are unchanged —
  a host that never calls the new method behaves exactly as today.
- The method is documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` alongside the delay options, stating
  the three anchor states (pending / visible / none) and the "appearance is gated by the
  dwell, following is not" rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `TooltipManager` exposes a public re-anchor method (`(x, y)`) that, while a show is pending, updates the pending anchor without restarting the dwell and without rendering.
- With an overlay already visible, the re-anchor method moves it to the new anchor immediately, using the same placement/clamping rules as `show()` (DOM viewport clamp and flip; Phaser container position), and does not re-render or re-create the overlay (no text reset, no destroy/create, no flicker).
- A re-anchor when nothing is pending and nothing is visible is a no-op: no overlay appears, no timer is scheduled, no content is rendered.
- With `SettingsPanel.showTooltips === false`, a re-anchor never makes a suppressed tooltip visible.
- Default behaviour is unchanged: with no delay configured (`delayMs`/`touchDelayMs` both 0) and no re-anchor call, rendering and timing are byte-for-byte identical to today, and every existing `TooltipManager` test passes unchanged.
- Unit tests in `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` cover: pending re-anchor does not restart the dwell; visible re-anchor repositions the DOM overlay (clamped/flipped) without changing its text; no-op when hidden; no-op when suppressed; Phaser-mode container reposition.
- Browser tests in `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` cover the delayed show followed by re-anchors inside the same target against a real Phaser scene (advanced clock, no real-time sleeps) — the overlay stays visible throughout and changes position with each re-anchor.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the re-anchor method, the three anchor states and the "dwell gates appearance, not following" rule; code comments in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` state the same contract.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A host can now keep a deliberately-summoned tooltip with the pointer as it moves across
the same target, so the tooltip feels attached to what it describes instead of freezing
where it first appeared.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager` (`show`, `renderNow`, `firePendingShow`,
  `cancelPendingShow`, `hide`, `hidePhaserTooltip`, `destroy`), the placement helpers
  (`computeViewportTooltipPosition`, `TOOLTIP_HOVER_OFFSET`) and the pending-show record.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — unit specs for the manager (delay, pending refresh,
  cancellation, suppression).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — browser specs against a real Phaser scene
  with an advanced clock.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the `TooltipManager` / hover-intent documentation section.

## Constraints

- **Additive only.** No change to `show()` timing semantics, no change to the 0 ms default
  and no new user-facing setting — the game item's AC8 requires the manager to be
  constructed with `delayMs`/`touchDelayMs` and nothing else.
- **No flicker.** Repositioning a visible overlay must not destroy or re-create the DOM
  node or the Phaser container, and must not reset its text.
- **No second dwell.** A re-anchor must never schedule a timer; the dwell is armed by
  `show()` for a new target only.
- **Placement parity.** DOM placement must keep the existing mapping and viewport
  clamp/flip, so a following tooltip cannot leave the viewport or jump on the edge.
- **Test cost is bounded.** No real-time sleeps in the suite; the browser specs advance
  Phaser's clock as the existing delayed-show specs do.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Unrelated to hover intent.** The re-anchor is a pure anchor operation; it must not
  become a "show without a dwell" back door. The no-op-when-hidden rule is the guard.
- **Placement duplication.** The DOM placement block in `renderNow` must be extracted
  into a shared private helper rather than copied, so the clamped/flipped position can
  never drift between the initial render and a re-anchor.
- **Phaser mode.** The container is created by `renderNow`; re-anchoring it is a
  `setPosition`, which is what a host-owned Phaser tooltip already expects.
- **Downstream consumer.** The Rising (`RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH`) will bump the `core`
  submodule to the release containing this method and call it from its hover router's
  "already shown" branch.

## Summary

Close the writer-facing authoring frictions measured by the Long Erasure spike, so a writer can add a branch to an existing story-line without retyping whole cells, guessing an authoring order, or dropping into the editor for prose.

Discovered-from: CG-0MWPY29730011FJ4 (GDD writer content pipeline, which documents each friction as a known limit and points here).

## The frictions (all re-verified at the GDD commit)

1. **Forward references are refused.** `storylines:author update-card` rejects an option naming a card that does not exist yet (`links to unknown card "gx-ghost"`), so a branch must be authored backwards from its target. `add-card` alone on an existing story-line can also flip the entry card and report every other card as `unreachable-card`.
2. **`update-card --options` replaces the whole cell.** Adding one option means retyping every existing option; a dropped `;` silently removes a branch until validation catches it.
3. **Every row repeats the full declared resource set.** The `resources` column is per-card, so the same key list is copied into every row; a mismatch is only caught downstream.
4. **No positional insert.** `add-card` appends, so CSV reading order drifts from narrative order.
5. **The author CLI cannot author prose.** `--field context=...` is refused ("field \"context\" is a mapped story-line column"), and the CLI has no `--context` / `--epilogue` flag, so prose can be authored only through the editor or its `--apply` bridge.

Mitigations that already exist (and must not regress): the editor's `add-linked-card` edit adds the card **and** the predecessor option in one validated transaction; stale content is refused; every diagnostic carries row, column and reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An option can be appended to an existing card without retyping the cell (an `add-option` author operation, or `add-linked-card` parity in the CLI).
- A writer can supply `--context` and `--epilogue` through `storylines:author` (`add-card` and `update-card`), or an equivalent documented path with no editor session.
- The resource key set is declared once per content file (or defaulted from a predecessor) instead of repeated per row, with the declared set still validated per card.
- `add-card` can insert at a documented position (append, or after a named card), and appending to an existing multi-member story-line cannot silently re-point the entry card.
- Forward-reference authoring has a documented, single-transaction path (author the option and its target together), so a branch is never half-authored.
- Each change is covered by unit tests over the author/edit seams, and the GDD's `§2.9` friction table is updated to "resolved" with the command that resolves it.
- `npm run build` and the unit profile are green.

## Key Files

- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — CLI flags and subcommands.
- `src/story-line/content/mutate.ts` — `addContentCard`, `updateContentCard`, spec shapes (already carry `context` / `epilogue`).
- `src/story-line/editor/edits.ts` — `add-linked-card` (the existing single-transaction precedent).
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — per-file resource declaration seam.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — authoring docs.
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §2.9 — the friction table this item closes out.

## Impact

A writer can add, edit and prose a story branch from the command line in one validated step instead of retyping whole cells or switching tools.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MWNHZ7DA00243HB** – Writer-authorable CSV option fields (completed)
- **CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S** – Storyline content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (completed)
- **CG-0MWO7EOJQ001090X** – Close coverage gap: A beat can author a `context` paragraph, per-option outcome prose and an ending epilogue **entire... (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, adapters, add, adding, adds (+168 more)
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: adapters, add, addcontentcard, adds, alone (+141 more)
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — matched: 0mwpy29730011fj4, acceptance, add, adding, adds (+137 more)

## Summary

Extend the authored-content route-space guard with a **scene-space mode** (`storylines:guard --manifest <file>`) that enumerates scene exits and beat refusals, and asserts two invariants: no exhausted close classifies as `success`, and no refusal leads to a state with no reachable ending.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.4 third static check (the clock is not a declared resource, so the content guard cannot see it).
- §2.8.6 item 5 (prove no scene exit strands the player) and §2.8 hull row (hull-costing doors stay survivable).
- §2.10 T3/T5 pacing evidence: a refusal or a hidden gate must never strand or silently truncate a run.
- §5.2 scene-space guard (named build-epic check).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` enumerates the playable route space of the **card chain** over declared resources (`gated-branch-survivable`, `ending-reachable`, `consequential-rejoin`).
- It has no manifest input, no scene boundary, no clock and no outcome/route semantics; the clock is not a declared resource, so a budget exhaustion is invisible to it.
- Bounds and clamping (G4) do not exist either, so a loss that clamps would currently enumerate differently from the authored intent.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Medium** (2-5 days): the nearest precedent is `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` itself (955 lines of bounded DFS with fail-closed truncation reporting) — this entry extends its state model with scene/clock/outcome, reusing its bound and reporting machinery.
- Band is medium because the enumeration machinery exists; the new work is state shape and the two invariants.

## Proposed shape

- Add a `--manifest` mode to `scripts/storyline-guard.ts`; keep the existing CSV mode unchanged.
- Enumerate (scene, beat, clock remaining, resources, outcome rules applied) states with the existing depth/state bounds; a bound hit stays a failure.
- Report per invariant, per scene exit and per refusal, in the existing JSON shape.
- Positive control required: a fixture whose exhausted close classifies `success` and a fixture whose refusal strands the player must both fail.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G3 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Give the declared resource set **bounds**: per-key min/max, spill at the maximum, clamped loss at the minimum, and a reported remainder. Deltas are applied through the declared projection, so every game with more than the `coins` / `reputation` pair gets the same guarantee.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 resource model: the ranges table (`hull` 0-5, `morale` 0-8, `stores` 0-6, `goodwill` 0-5, `charge` 1-2), the "surplus spills, loss clamps" behaviour and the failure state per key.
- §2.10 tension design (a clamped loss at zero must be recorded, not silently ignored).
- §2.8.6 item 1 (bounds and clamping are named gaps) and item 2 (bounds become manifest data, owned with G2).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `createResourceProjection(...).applyResourceDelta` in `src/story-line/resources.ts` forwards every finite, non-zero delta to the game's field mutator with no bounds: a gain past a cap banks, a loss below zero goes negative, and nothing is reported.
- `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` (same module) is a value bag, not a bounds declaration.
- The nearest constrained-resource helper, `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, is hard-coded to `coins` / `reputation` and exposes only `minCoins` / `minReputation` (no maximum, no spill, no clamped-loss record).

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small-medium** (1-3 days): the nearest precedent is `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts` (constraint-checked deltas) and the `StorylineResourceProjection` seam in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small-medium because the seam and its tests exist; the work is a bounds type, clamp/spill arithmetic, a reported remainder and propagation through the GDD's manifest data (G2).

## Proposed shape

- `StorylineResourceBounds = Readonly<Record<key, { min: number; max: number }>>`.
- `applyResourceDelta` returns (or reports through a callback) `{ applied, spilled, clamped }` per key; never silently discards.
- Absent bounds keep today's unbounded behaviour, so no existing game changes.
- Unit tests: spill at max, clamp at min, multi-key delta ordering, absent bounds backward compatibility.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G4 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.
data.title: Engine gap: resource bounds, spill and clamped loss

## Summary

Make **irreversibility** an engine guarantee: a declared irreversible resource key can never be granted by an option `#extra` or a manifest loss rule, and the refusal is a hard authoring error, not an authoring convention.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 `hull` as the irreversible tension dial (0-5, no recovery within a run).
- §2.10 irreversible-loss tension and the reset ending's structural recovery.
- §2.8.6 item 6 (`#extra=hull:1` is legal content today).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `resources.irreversible` is manifest data read only by the proposed manifest validator rule `loss-not-irreversible` (GDD §2.4); the manifest validator itself does not exist (G2).
- Nothing in `src/story-line/resources.ts` knows the concept: `selectDeclaredDelta` filters undeclared keys only (`ignored`), so a grant to a declared irreversible key is applied.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` refuses `unknown-resource-key` (a key outside the declared set) but cannot refuse a *direction* on a declared key.
- The GDD's guard is a fixture test plus authoring discipline (GDD §2.8.3/§2.8.6), which is the gap this entry closes.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the `unknown-resource-key` rule in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` (a declarative, row + column + reason diagnostic) plus the `selectDeclaredDelta` sign handling in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one declaration, one validation rule and one guard in the projection.

## Proposed shape

- Declare irreversible keys alongside the declared set (`StorylineResourceProjection` option or manifest data).
- Reject a positive delta to an irreversible key at authoring time (validator code, e.g. `irreversible-grant`) and at resolution time (refuse, log).
- Unit tests: a `#extra=hull:1` row fails validation with the row/column reason; a negative hull cost still applies.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G5 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

**Surface affordability** instead of deleting it: compile an unaffordable option into a requirement object (which keys, how much is needed, how much the player has) so a presenting layer can render it disabled with its shortfall, rather than omitting it at draw time.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.3/§2.9 "an unaffordable option is not shown" — the presentation contract must say why.
- §2.8.6 item 3 (measured cost: 32 of 302 option instances hidden; 107 of 197 dead turns gate-collapsed).
- §3.6 B4 affordability presentation; §2.10 T5 (hidden affordability is not tension).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `isOptionAffordable(option, resources, declaredResources)` in `src/story-line/compile.ts` returns a boolean.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` filters unaffordable options out of `compiledOptions` at draw time, so the presenting layer never sees them; there is no requirement/shortfall shape anywhere in the compiled option model.
- `StorylineOption` (in `src/story-line/types.ts`) carries the `cost` declaration but no computed affordability state.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is `isOptionAffordable` itself plus the compiled-option shape in `src/story-line/compile.ts`; the arithmetic exists, only the output shape changes.
- Band is small because it is an additive field on the compiled option and a policy switch (omit vs surface), with no new evaluator.

## Proposed shape

- `OptionAffordability = { affordable: true } | { affordable: false; shortfall: Array<{ key; required; available }> }`.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` gains a policy option (`'omit'` default, preserving every current caller and test; `'surface'` keeps the option with its affordability state).
- Resolution still refuses an unaffordable option (unchanged), so surfacing cannot create an illegal play path.
- Unit tests: default policy unchanged; surface policy yields the shortfall per key; an unaffordable surfaced option cannot resolve.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G7 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Add **act/scene transition presentation**: a scene-exit banner (act title, scene title, objective result) and a sequenced act transition (banner -> objective outcome -> route) with a reduced-motion fallback. The camera-level transition helper already ships; the banner surface and the sequence do not.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.3 step D (scene close -> next beat) and §3.1 `sceneBanner` zone.
- §3.6 B5 act/scene transition presentation; §3.2 overlay/sequence behaviour.
- §2.10 pacing: the exit is where the player reads what the scene cost them.
- §3.3 audio mapping for the act/scene transition SFX.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/ui/sceneTransition.ts` already provides `runSceneTransition` (camera fade/slide with a reduced-motion skip) — so a camera transition is **not** the gap.
- What does not exist: any banner/act-title presentation surface, any sequence that presents the scene outcome before routing, and any rendered precedent for a scene boundary. The spike has no scene boundary (`example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts`) and its layout declares six zones with no `sceneBanner` (`example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json`: `statusBar, narrative, options, feedback, journal, controls`).
- No component in `src/ui/index.ts` composes a title + outcome + advance into a timed surface; `runSceneTransition` animates the camera only and resolves a promise.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small-medium** (1-3 days): the nearest precedents are `src/ui/sceneTransition.ts` (timed transition with reduced-motion fallback), `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts` (sequenced animated text with SFX and a skip path) and `src/ui/Overlay.ts` (`createOverlayBackground` / `dismissOverlay` depth conventions).
- Band is small-medium because every primitive exists; the work is composition, SLL zone wiring, SFX and a reduced-motion path.

## Proposed shape

- `presentSceneExit(scene, { actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route, reducedMotion, soundManager })` resolving when the banner is dismissed (auto-advance or click).
- Reduced motion: no slide/fade, a single immediate state with the same information.
- Outcome text and colour-independent channel (printed `success` / `partial` / `failure` word), never colour alone.
- Unit/browser tests: sequence order, skip path, reduced-motion path, SFX key selection from `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G9 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Retire the legacy **`act` / `clockCost` CSV columns** now that act membership and pacing are beat-sheet data: remove them from the Gym content adapter, migrate the remaining rows, and add the migration check that refuses a disagreeing manifest/CSV pair while both exist.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.1 composition contract (act membership is `scene.id`; pacing is `beat.clockCost` in the manifest).
- §2.9 "the two retired columns" and §2.4 `clock-cost-mismatch` (migration-only rule).
- §2.9.7 friction 5 (act/clock as generic `--field` writes).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` declares `act` and `clockCost` as Gym game columns and lists both in `editableColumns` (with defaults `I` / `1`), so authors can still write beat-sheet data into the wrong place.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` reads `clockCost` per beat for its pressure clock.
- The migration check (`clock-cost-mismatch`) only becomes possible once the manifest validator exists (G2), so this entry depends on it.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the adapter column declaration/removal itself in `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` plus the `missing-column` diagnostic in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts`.
- Band is small because it is a content-format change with a migration, not new machinery; the validator rule is the only new logic.

## Proposed shape

- Migrate the spike's `act` / `clockCost` values into the episode manifest (Appendix A carries the same data).
- Remove both columns from the adapter and `editableColumns`; the spike's rule module reads the manifest instead.
- While both forms exist, the manifest validator rejects a disagreeing pair (`clock-cost-mismatch`); once removed, the content validator refuses the columns as unknown.
- Unit tests: CSV with the retired column fails loudly; manifest/CSV agreement passes; mismatch fails.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G10 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Add **keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order**: number/arrow navigation of the option list with Enter/Space activation, focus traversal inside an open overlay, and Escape closing only the topmost modal — so the keyboard path in the GDD's accessibility contract is real rather than aspirational.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.4 keyboard and touch input paths.
- §3.6 B7; §3.8 (the keyboard path is untestable until this lands).
- §3.2 overlay behaviour (exactly one modal live, Escape closes the topmost).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- Only the panels' own toggle keys are bound: `HelpPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `FORWARD_SLASH` = `?`) and `SettingsPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `Escape`) register their own `keydown` listeners (`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`).
- `getEndTurnKeybind()` / `setEndTurnKeybind()` in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` bind exactly one game action.
- No choice-list navigator, focus-trap or focus-order helper is exported from `src/ui/index.ts`.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedents are the `keydown` listener lifecycle in `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` (register/off on destroy) and `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` (one live modal, ordered open/close) + `src/ui/Overlay.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one navigator helper plus focus handling on the existing overlay primitives.

## Proposed shape

- `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, { count, onChoose, keys? })` — `1`-`6` and arrows + Enter/Space, disabled while a modal is open.
- `attachOverlayFocus(scene, overlayObjects, { onEscape })` — traversal order, activation, Escape topmost-only.
- Both return a disposer, and both respect reduced motion/no-ops in headless tests.
- Unit tests: index keys select the right option; arrow wrap; Escape closes only the topmost; disposer removes listeners.

## Source

## Summary

Add a **shared verbosity preference** (Full / Concise) to `SettingsStore` and `SettingsPanel`, so the GDD's verbosity toggle persists across games and sessions instead of being a game-local `extraToggles` switch.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.2 verbosity and tooltips (the Full/Concise toggle).
- §3.6 B8.
- §3.4 accessibility: a shared, persistent reading-comfort preference.

- `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity('full' | 'concise')` with a storage key and a safe fallback when storage is unavailable (mirror `getTooltips`).

## Goal

As a producer, I want test-generated artefacts to stay out of the working tree, so that the dev-push full-suite gate is never discarded as `state_changed_during_run` simply because a browser test produced an attachment.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` runs the full suite in the item's worktree and discards the verdict when the checkout's `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` surface changes mid-run (`snapshot_own_checkout` / `state_changed_during_run`, SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE). Vitest 4's browser projects write `context.annotate` attachments to `<root>/.vitest-attachments/` (default `attachmentsDir`). That directory is **not** in `.gitignore`, so any run that produces an attachment (observed: the same 102 KB PNG, deterministic across two runs) leaves an untracked path behind, the fingerprint differs before/after, and the gate reports `full_suite_red` / `reason: infrastructure` — nothing is committed or pushed and the item is released to `open`.

Observed on this checkout during `CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9` (two consecutive finishes, same hash). Workaround used locally: added `.vitest-attachments/` to `.git/info/exclude` (local, untracked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.vitest-attachments/` (and any other root-level Vitest attachment output) is ignored repo-wide, either by adding it to `.gitignore` or by pinning `attachmentsDir` outside the repo in `vite.config.ts`.
- A full-suite run that produces an attachment leaves `git status --porcelain` unchanged, so `implement.py finish` is not discarded as `state_changed_during_run`.
- The chosen fix is recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (testing section) if it changes the developer workflow.

## Notes

`discovered-from:CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`. Low risk, XS effort. The local `.git/info/exclude` workaround is not shared with other clones or CI, so this item exists to fix it at the repo level.


## Impact

A browser test that writes a Vitest attachment no longer silently discards a green full-suite verdict, so a finished change reaches `dev` instead of failing as an unexplained infrastructure red.
data.title: Ignore Vitest browser attachments so the dev-push state-change guard is not tripped

Run the human browser playtest the GDD recommends (ideally three people, at least one who has not read the content) over the v1 Long Erasure content, and record measured wall-clock run durations, phone-screen readability and felt tension.

## Why

The v1 scope statement (CG-0MWPY2HJU006LJMU, GDD §7.2) estimates playtime at 13 minutes a run (10–16 range) from the measured beats-per-run figure (spike: 6–10 beats, mean 8.48) multiplied by two stated, unmeasured assumptions: 35–50 s a beat (A1) and ~3 min presentation overhead (A2). This playtest is the measurement that replaces A1 and A2. It also closes the evidence limit recorded in GDD §2.6 (agent-driven structural measurement, not felt enjoyment) and lifts deferral D3 of the GDD's deferred list (§7.6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Three participants (at least one who has not read the content) each play at least one complete run in a browser, with wall-clock duration recorded from opening to epilogue.
- The measured durations are compared with the 10–16 minute range and the 13-minute target; the difference and its cause are recorded.
- Phone-screen readability (or a named proxy viewport) is assessed and any blocking issue is filed as its own work item.
- Findings are recorded in docs/design/storyline-playtest-evaluation.md and the playtime basis in GDD §7.2 is updated or confirmed.

## Impact

A producer can replace the v1 playtime estimate's two unmeasured assumptions with measured human run durations.

## Provenance

Discovered from CG-0MWPY2HJU006LJMU (GDD v1 scope statement and deferred list), deferral D3.

## Goal

As a player of the Gym story-line demo, I want each option button to show what
it costs, so that a cost-bearing choice (`#cost=coins:5`) is visible before I
commit to it rather than only in the activity log afterwards.

## Impact

A player now sees what a choice costs on the button itself (`Invest — 5 coins`),
so a pricey option is no longer a surprise in the activity log after the fact.

## Background

`GymStorylineScene` renders each compiled option as `[ <label> ]`, so the
authored `#cost` on `Invest` is invisible at the point of choice. The content
now drives the demo (CG-0MWRSOU91003P36J), so this is a presentation gap, not a
data gap: `StorylineOption.cost` already carries the authored cost map.

## Approach

- Add a game-agnostic formatter to the shared story-line UI adapter
  (`src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts`): `formatOptionCost(cost)` and
  `formatOptionLabel(option)`, so every game renders costs the same way instead
  of re-implementing string building.
- `formatOptionLabel` returns the bare label when the option authors no cost,
  and `<label> — <n> <key>[, <n> <key>]` when it does (keys in declaration
  order, resource keys quoted as authored — the engine has no plural rules for
  arbitrary resource keys).
- Use it in `GymStorylineScene` for the button text.
- Documentation: the story-line reference documents the formatter and the demo's
  option rendering; the scene's help text mentions that costs are shown.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `formatOptionCost` / `formatOptionLabel` are exported from the story-line
      public surface and unit-tested: no cost → bare label; single cost;
      multiple resources in declaration order; a cost-bearing option keeps its
      label text intact.
- [ ] `GymStorylineScene` renders `Invest` as `[ Invest — 5 coins ]` and
      `Ignore` (no cost) unchanged as `[ Ignore ]`.
- [ ] The Gym storyline browser test asserts the cost-bearing label (derived
      from the CSV catalogue, not a hard-coded literal) and the cost-free label.
- [ ] `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the formatter, and the scene
      help text tells the player costs are shown on the button.
- [ ] Build and the affected test profiles pass; `storylines:validate` and
      `storylines:graph -- --check` stay green.

## Key Files

- `src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts` — the shared formatter (`formatOptionCost`, `formatOptionLabel`).
- `src/story-line/index.ts` — public re-export of the new helpers.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` — renders the option buttons and its help text.
- `tests/story-line/ui-adapter.test.ts` — unit coverage for the formatter.
- `tests/gym/GymStorylineScene.browser.test.ts` — scene-level label assertions.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — documents the option-label formatter.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 step A: entering a beat charges its `clockCost` against the scene's remaining clock, presents it, and refuses a beat that cannot be afforded — closing the scene with `budget-exhausted` before any option is presented.

## Scope

- `enterBeat(cardId)` on the runner: refusal check, charge, and a returned entry record (`cardId`, `clockCost`, `clockRemaining`) so the caller can render the card's `context` prose and the scene banner.
- `budgetExhausted` flag set by a refusal and carried into the scene close.
- The options the caller presents come from `storyline.getStorylineOptions` gated by `isOptionAffordable` — the runner does not filter or re-derive affordability itself.
- A requested entry that is already unaffordable drives the close path handed to the next feature (scene close), not a partial entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Beat entry matches §2.3 step A: an affordable beat is charged and presented, and the entry record reports the charged cost and the post-charge `clockRemaining`.
- A beat whose cost exactly equals the remaining clock is affordable, leaves `clockRemaining` at 0, and is reported as presented (spending the last tick is legal).
- A beat whose `clockCost` exceeds the remaining clock is refused, never played, its options are never presented, and it closes the scene with `budgetExhausted = true` and reason `budget-exhausted`.
- One test per clause above, registered against the §2.3 step map entry for A.2 / A.3.
- Beat entry consumes no RNG: the adapter double's RNG call count is unchanged across an affordable entry and across a refusal.
- The "Episode runner → Beat entry" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the refusal rule and the exact-cost clause.

## Minimal Implementation

- `enterBeat` reads `Beat.clockCost` from the validated manifest, compares against `sceneClockRemaining`, charges or refuses, and returns an immutable entry record.
- Refusal sets `budgetExhausted` on the run state and reports reason `budget-exhausted`; presenting options stays the caller's step.
- Three tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-beat-entry.test.ts` (affordable, exact-cost, refused) plus one RNG-accounting test.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the public surface and types (`Episode runner public types and exports`).

## Deliverables

- `enterBeat` implementation, its tests, and its documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs `enterBeat`, the charge/refusal logic and the entry record.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — Existing `Beat` / `Scene.budget` shapes read by the charge step.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — Existing affordability projection used for the presented option gate.
- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-beat-entry.test.ts` — Needs one test per §2.3 step A clause plus the RNG-accounting test.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Beat entry" subsection.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 step B: the player's option resolves through `@story-line` unchanged, and the runner classifies the pushed card into "continue the scene" or "close the scene with this pending chain" — the boundary rule that makes the beat set the scene boundary.

## Scope

- `resolveChoice(option)` on the runner: delegate to `storyline.resolveStorylineOption`, then classify `pushedCard`.
- Classification: in-scene beat → continue at that beat; out-of-scene beat → close with `pendingChain = pushedCard`; ending card → close with `pendingChain = pushedCard`; no pushed card → close with `pendingChain = null`.
- The runner never re-reads an `options` cell, re-implements successor precedence or keeps a second declared key set (constraint: one choice model).
- The returned classification record names the case and the pending chain so the scene close and the tests read one shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Choice resolution delegates to `storyline.resolveStorylineOption` for every case, asserted with a spy on the storyline double — the runner contains no second resolution path.
- An in-scene pushed card continues the scene: the runner reports `next: "continue"` and leaves the run state inside the same scene.
- An out-of-scene pushed card closes the scene with `pendingChain` set to that card id and `next: "close"`.
- An ending card pushed by a choice closes the scene with `pendingChain` set to the ending card id and `next: "close"`.
- A resolution that pushes no card closes the scene with `pendingChain = null` and `next: "close"`.
- One test per `pushedCard` case (in-scene beat, out-of-scene beat, ending card, none), registered against the §2.3 step map B.5 entries.

## Minimal Implementation

- `resolveChoice` calls `storyline.resolveStorylineOption(state, card, option)`, then a pure `classifyPushedCard` helper reading the manifest's assigned-card index and `manifest.endings`.
- The classification is a discriminated union (`continue` / `close`) with `pendingChain` set only on the close cases.
- Four tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-choice.test.ts`, each naming its case.

## Dependencies

- Depends on beat entry (`Episode runner beat entry: clock charge and refusal`) — a choice is always made from an entered beat.

## Deliverables

- `resolveChoice` + `classifyPushedCard` implementation, four classification tests, documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs `resolveChoice` and the pure `classifyPushedCard` helper.
- `src/story-line/resolve.ts` — Existing `resolveStorylineOption` the runner delegates to (read-only).
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — Existing `Beat` / `endings` data the classifier indexes.
- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-choice.test.ts` — Needs the four `pushedCard` case tests.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Choice resolution and scene boundary" subsection.

## Summary

Implement the loss ledger of §2.2.8: chain losses observed by diffing `engine.getResources` across a beat resolution, and rule losses applied at scene close — both recorded with the GDD's field names, never as a positive line, and never as arithmetic of the runner's own.

## Scope

- Chain-loss diffing: snapshot the irreversible keys before a choice resolves, diff after, and record one `{ kind: "chain", sceneId, beatId, field, delta }` per negative net change.
- Rule-loss recording seam used by scene close: `{ kind: "rule", sceneId, ruleId, field, delta, statement }` appended in declaration order.
- The ledger is read-only to callers (`getLossLedger()`), ordered by observation, JSON-safe.
- The runner performs no resource arithmetic: every observed delta is what `engine.applyResourceDelta` applied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The loss ledger records chain entries for negative net irreversible deltas observed across a beat resolution, carrying the GDD's field names (`kind`, `sceneId`, `beatId`, `field`, `delta`).
- A net positive (refund) change on an irreversible key records nothing — the ledger never contains a positive `delta` line.
- A fired loss rule records a rule entry (`kind: "rule"`, `sceneId`, `ruleId`, `field`, `delta`, `statement`) in declaration order.
- Ledger lines are appended in observation order and exposed read-only; mutating the returned array does not change runner state.
- No loss line is recorded unless a corresponding `engine.applyResourceDelta` call was made (asserted against the adapter double's delta recorder).
- The ledger survives a JSON round-trip unchanged (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(lines))` deep-equals the original).

## Minimal Implementation

- A `lossLedger` array in run state plus an internal `recordChainLoss` / `recordRuleLoss` pair; both are pure appends.
- The chain diff wraps the choice resolution: read the irreversible-key subset of `engine.getResources`, resolve, read again, record negatives.
- Tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-loss-ledger.test.ts` using a card that applies an irreversible cost and one that grants a refund.

## Dependencies

- Depends on choice resolution classification (`Episode runner choice resolution and pendingChain`), which brackets the diff window.

## Deliverables

- Ledger recording implementation, chain-diff wrapper, tests, documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs the ledger array, the chain diff and both record seams.
- `src/story-line/types.ts` — Needs `LossLedgerEntry` refined into its `chain` / `rule` variants.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — Existing `engine` resource projection and `selectDeclaredDelta` helper the diff reads through.
- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-loss-ledger.test.ts` — Needs chain-loss, refund, rule-loss, ordering and round-trip tests.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Loss ledger" subsection with the two entry shapes.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 steps C.6–C.8: evaluate the scene objective once against post-resolution resources, classify the outcome first-match-wins from the authored rules (including an authored `budget: "exhausted"` rule), and apply every matching loss rule through the engine seam.

## Scope

- Objective evaluation: `check` against `engine.getResources` after the resolving choice, absent keys reading 0, recorded as `objectiveMet`.
- Outcome classification: first matching `outcomeRule` in declaration order over `{ objective }`, `{ budget }` and raw `{ field, op, value }` conditions; the catch-all guarantees totality (no defensive fallback in code).
- Loss-rule application: every matching `losses` rule in declaration order through `engine.applyResourceDelta`, one ledger rule line and one `engine.appendLog` line per rule (statement plus signed amount and key).
- `budgetExhausted` is classified by the authored table, never hard-coded to `failure`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scene close matches §2.3 steps C.6–C.9: the objective is evaluated exactly once, against post-resolution resources; classification is first-match-wins in declaration order and honours an authored `{ budget: "exhausted" }` rule placed before the catch-all; every matching loss rule is applied through `engine.applyResourceDelta` in declaration order, producing one ledger line and one activity-log line each.
- Classification is first-match-wins in declaration order and honours an authored `{ budget: "exhausted" }` rule placed before the catch-all, so a refused close in `s-iii-core` classifies `failure` through `watch-spent`.
- Every matching loss rule is applied through `engine.applyResourceDelta` in declaration order, producing one ledger rule line and one activity-log line each (statement plus signed amount and key).
- No rule may throw on a manifest that passed `validateEpisodeManifest`: the classifier has no defensive catch-all, and a fixture-wide sweep over every scene × outcome × objective/budget combination completes without throwing.
- `engine.getResources` is read exactly once for the objective per close (asserted with a counting adapter).
- The "Scene close" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the classification order and the `budget: "exhausted"` convention.

## Minimal Implementation

- `closeScene(reason)` performing objective evaluation, outcome classification and loss application in that order, returning the classified outcome + rule id.
- A pure `evaluateSceneCondition(condition, { objectiveMet, budgetExhausted, resources })` helper shared with routing (`when` gates).
- Tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-scene-close.test.ts` covering objective met/unmet, declaration-order precedence, exhausted-rule precedence, multi-loss ordering, and the no-throw sweep.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the loss ledger (`Episode runner loss ledger: chain and rule entries`) for rule-loss lines, and on beat refusal (`Episode runner beat entry: clock charge and refusal`) for `budgetExhausted`.

## Deliverables

- Scene-close implementation, condition evaluator, tests, documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs `closeScene`, the objective evaluation and loss application.
- `src/story-line/types.ts` — Needs the close-result and condition-context types.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — Existing `Objective`, `OutcomeRule`, `SceneCondition`, `LossRule` shapes consumed read-only.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — Existing declared-resource projection the objective reads.
- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-scene-close.test.ts` — Needs objective, precedence, exhausted, multi-loss and no-throw tests.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Scene close" subsection.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 steps C.9–C.12: select the first matching route in declaration order, resolve its `chain` / `beat` / `ending` target, emit the nine-field `scene-exit` record, and enter the target scene with a fresh clock, an appended history entry and irreversible keys untouched.

## Scope

- Route selection: first route where `on` matches (`*` or the outcome) **and** `when` is absent-or-matching **and** the route is not a `chain` route while `pendingChain` is null.
- Target resolution: `chain` → the pending chain card; `beat` with explicit `beat` → that card; `beat` without → the target scene's `entryBeat`; `ending` → present the ending card and close the run.
- `scene-exit` emission: exactly `{ sceneId, objectiveMet, outcome, ruleId, routeId, clockSpent, clockRemaining, budgetExhausted, nextBeat }`, appended once per close in close order.
- Scene entry: reset the clock to the target scene's `budget.clock`, push the scene id onto `sceneHistory` (route id onto `routeHistory`), clear `pendingChain`, leave every irreversible key unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Routing matches §2.3 steps C.9–C.12: the first matching route in declaration order wins, honouring `on` and `when`; a `chain` route is skipped when `pendingChain` is null.
- `chain`, `beat` (with and without an explicit `beat`) and `ending` targets each resolve correctly, with a `beat` target without a beat opening the target scene's `entryBeat`.
- Entering a scene resets `sceneClockRemaining` to its `budget.clock`, pushes the scene id onto `sceneHistory` (and the route id onto `routeHistory`), clears `pendingChain`, and leaves irreversible resource keys unchanged.
- The `scene-exit` record carries exactly the nine fields of §2.3 step 11 and is the single source the journal/banner data is derived from; it is appended once per scene close and never rewritten.
- An `ending` target presents the ending card and closes the run, and the reset ending's restart action returns the run to `start`.
- Route selection, scene entry and `scene-exit` emission consume no RNG (adapter RNG call count unchanged across a full scripted scene close).

## Minimal Implementation

- `selectRoute(outcome, context)`, `resolveRouteTarget(target)`, `emitSceneExit(...)` and `enterScene(sceneId, beatId)` as pure-ish helpers on the runner; the run state is the only mutation target.
- `sceneHistory` / `routeHistory` arrays in run state; `sceneExits` array exposed read-only.
- Tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-routing.test.ts`, including a route-order test that reorders two candidate routes in an in-memory manifest copy and asserts the decision flips.

## Dependencies

- Depends on scene close (`Episode runner scene close: objective, outcome and losses`) for the outcome and rule id the route reads.

## Deliverables

- Routing, scene entry, `scene-exit` emission, tests, documentation subsection with the nine-field table.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs route selection, target resolution, `scene-exit` emission and scene entry.
- `src/story-line/types.ts` — Needs `SceneExitRecord` and the route-history entry shape.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — Existing `SceneRoute`, `RouteTarget`, `Act` / `Scene` shapes consumed read-only.
- `src/story-line/journal.ts` — Existing activity-log vocabulary the scene-exit and route log lines join.
- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-routing.test.ts` — Needs route-order, chain-skip, target-resolution, entry-reset and RNG-accounting tests.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Routing and scene entry" subsection and the nine-field `scene-exit` table.

## Summary

Persist and resume the run through `serializeWithVersion` / `deserializeWithVersion` with the runner's own `schemaVersion`, covering the nine in-scope run-state fields, and refusing a version mismatch rather than loading best-effort.

## Scope

- An `EpisodeRunStateSerializer` at `schemaVersion: 1` (no `migrate` hook in v1, so a mismatch is a refusal).
- The nine persisted fields: `seed`, `currentActId`, `currentSceneId`, `currentBeatId`, `sceneClockRemaining`, `pendingChain`, `sceneHistory`, `routeHistory`, `lossLedger`.
- A `serialize()` / `restore(payload)` pair on the runner built on the core `SaveLoad` helpers; `resources` and the journal stay `@story-line`'s own state (out of scope, per the epic's bounded persistence AC).
- Resume continues the same scene clock and produces the same next entry resolution as the live run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Versioned run state round-trips through `serializeWithVersion` / `deserializeWithVersion` with all nine persisted fields of §3.5.2 preserved: `seed`, `currentActId`, `currentSceneId`, `currentBeatId`, `sceneClockRemaining`, `pendingChain`, `sceneHistory`, `routeHistory`, `lossLedger` — and a version mismatch is refused rather than best-effort loaded.
- A version mismatch is refused rather than best-effort loaded: `deserializeWithVersion` throws the core incompatible-version error and the runner restores no partial state.
- A restored runner resumes mid-scene: its `sceneClockRemaining` matches the saved value and the next beat entry charges from it (no clock reset on restore).
- A restored runner's ledger deep-equals the saved ledger, so a reload is not a refund.
- Serialising and restoring consumes no RNG and applies no resource delta (adapter double assertions).
- The "Persistence" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` lists the nine persisted fields and the refusal behaviour.

## Minimal Implementation

- `serializeRunState(runnerState)` / `hydrateRunState(payload, manifest)` pure functions plus the `SaveSerializer` object; the runner exposes `serialize()` and `createEpisodeRunner({ ..., restored })`.
- Tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-persistence.test.ts`: round-trip, version-mismatch refusal, mid-scene resume, ledger fidelity and no-side-effect assertions.

## Dependencies

- Depends on routing and the `scene-exit` record (`Episode runner routing, scene entry and scene-exit record`), which fixes the shape of the state being persisted.

## Deliverables

- Serializer plus hydrate path, runner `serialize()` / restored construction, persistence tests, documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — Needs `serialize()`, restored construction and the hydrate path.

## Summary

Prove the whole thing on the committed worked manifest: play the `long-erasure` episode end-to-end through the runner, reaching all four endings, forcing a `budget-exhausted` close in `s-iii-core` that classifies `failure` and applies `hull-sacrificed`, and exercising the reset ending's restart.

## Scope

- A scripted-choice driver over the committed fixture (no game module, no rendering) that plays a full run through the public `@story-line` surface plus the runner.
- Four ending routes, each asserted by ending card id.
- A forced budget-exhausted close in `s-iii-core` (`le-iii-approach` costs 3 of a 5-tick clock, `le-iii-ahead` costs 3 → refused) that classifies `failure` via `watch-spent` and applies `hull-sacrificed`.
- The `le-end-reset` restart action returning the run to `start` with irreversible keys left at their lost values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The committed acceptance fixture plays end-to-end: `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json` + `long-erasure.csv` validate clean (via the delivered `validateEpisodeManifest`) and a unit test drives the runner along routes reaching all four endings, asserted by ending card id.
- One scripted run forces a `budget-exhausted` close in `s-iii-core` that classifies `failure` and applies `hull-sacrificed`: exactly one `hull` rule-loss ledger line and `hull` reduced by 1 through `engine.applyResourceDelta`.
- The reset ending's restart action returns the run to `start` (act, scene and beat equal the manifest's `start`) and leaves irreversible keys at their lost values rather than restoring them.
- Every scene exit produced by the four runs matched a manifest route and a manifest outcome rule — no exit carries an undefined `routeId` or `ruleId`, and no run throws.
- The suite imports the runner and `@story-line` surface only — it does not import `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` or any other game module.
- The "Acceptance fixture" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` records the four-ending walkthrough and the refused-close arithmetic.

## Minimal Implementation

- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-fixture.test.ts` with a small `playChoices(runner, storyline, steps)` helper plus four scripted routes and one refusal script.
- Reuse the harness fixture loader and adapter double from the first child; no new fixture copy (Assumption A3).

## Summary

Prove and pin determinism: the runner consumes no RNG outside the seeded `@story-line` candidate draw, and two runs at the same seed with the same choice sequence produce identical scene exits, ledger lines and final outcome.

## Scope

- An RNG-accounting test across a full scripted run: every draw is attributable to option resolution, none to entry, close, classification, loss application or routing.
- A same-seed/same-choices comparison over two independently constructed runners producing identical ordered `scene-exit` records, ledger lines and final outcome.
- A source-scan test asserting no `Math.random` occurrence in the runner module.
- A table-order sensitivity test documenting that reordering a route table is the only lever that changes a decision at a fixed seed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Determinism is proven by test: two runs with the same seed and the same choice sequence produce identical ordered `scene-exit` records, identical ledger lines and the same final outcome.
- No RNG is consumed by beat entry, scene close, outcome classification, loss application or routing — asserted by an RNG-call ledger that attributes every draw to an option resolution.
- `Math.random` does not appear in `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (source-scan test), and no `Date.now()` / timestamp enters the scene-exit record or the ledger.
- Reordering two competing routes in an in-memory manifest copy flips the decision — the only lever at a fixed seed — while an unmodified copy reproduces byte-identical records after JSON serialisation.
- The "Determinism" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` states the one-RNG rule and links the tests that pin it.

## Minimal Implementation

- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-determinism.test.ts` with a double that records every `rng(state)` call tagged with the pipeline stage the runner reports.
- A JSON-normalised comparison helper for record arrays; no new production code beyond the stage tag on the RNG plumbing if the adapter double needs it.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the worked-manifest acceptance suite (`Episode runner worked-manifest acceptance suite`), which supplies the scripted runs.

## Deliverables

- Determinism test suite, documentation subsection.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-determinism.test.ts` — Needs the same-seed, RNG-attribution, source-scan and table-order tests.
- `tests/story-line/helpers/episode-fixture.ts` — Existing adapter double extended with an RNG call ledger.
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — The module under the `Math.random` / determinism guard.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — Needs the "Determinism" subsection.
